  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:

          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'

        title:

          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true

          format: date-time

## Change: global `customerCode` assignment

New owners get a `customerCode` formatted `<LAST3>-<NNNN>` — the upper-cased first three letters of the last name, a hyphen, and a 4-digit zero-padded sequence equal to one more than the current owner count (e.g. `SMI-0007`). It's assigned once at registration and persisted, so it stays stable on later reads.

## Files touched, and why each

- **`service/CustomerCodeGenerator.java`** (new) — a small component with a single responsibility: produce the code for an owner. It owns both the sequence source (`ownerRepository.count() + 1`) and the `<LAST3>-<NNNN>` format. Kept out of the `ClinicServiceImpl` facade so that class doesn't accumulate formatting logic.
- **`service/ClinicServiceImpl.java`** — `saveOwner` now delegates to the generator, but only for a brand-new owner without a code (`owner.isNew() && getCustomerCode() == null`), so updates never regenerate it. Injected the generator via the constructor.
- **`model/Owner.java`** — added the persisted `customerCode` field (`customer_code` column) with getter/setter.
- **`repository/OwnerRepository.java`** + **`jdbc`/`jpa` impls** — added `count()`. Spring Data JPA (the active profile) derives it automatically; the other two implementations got explicit `COUNT` queries so everything compiles.
- **`resources/openapi.yml`** — added `customerCode` as a read-only string on the `Owner` response schema. This regenerates `OwnerDto` with the field, which MapStruct auto-maps by name — no mapper change needed. It's absent from `OwnerFields` (the input), so it can't be client-supplied.
- **`db/{h2,hsqldb,mysql,postgres}/schema.sql`** — added the `customer_code` column to each owners table (tests run on hsqldb).

The acceptance test (`coreFormatAndGlobalSequence`) verifies the `SMI-`/`JON-` prefixes and that the two owners' sequence numbers are consecutive — both pass, and the full suite is green.
